paite: Zingchiang thu ah ki- uangsak ke'n; ni in bang hon suahpih ding ahia chih lah na thei ngal kei a.
english: Don’t boast about tomorrow; for you don’t know what a day may bring.

paite: Midang in nang hon phat uhen, nangmah mah kam hilou in; mikhual in nangmah mah mukte hilou in.
english: Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth; a stranger, and not your own lips.

paite: Suang agik a, piaunel agik hi; himahleh mihai lungzinna huaite gel sang in agikzaw hi.
english: A stone is heavy, and sand is a burden; but a fool’s provocation is heavier than both.

paite: Thangpaihna agilou, hehna akhel; himahleh thikna ma ah kua adingh thei dia?
english: Wrath is cruel, and anger is overwhelming; but who is able to stand before jealousy?

paite: Aguk a itna sang in alangtang a salhna ahoihzaw.
english: Better is open rebuke than hidden love.

paite: Lawm khat liamnate ginom ahi ua, himahleh melma hon tawpna khemna ahi.
english: The wounds of a friend are faithful, although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.

paite: Kha gilvah in khuaikhak achimtak a; himahleh kha gilkial a ding in thil kha chiteng akhum hi.
english: A full soul loathes a honeycomb; but to a hungry soul, every bitter thing is sweet.

paite: Abuk a kipan a vasa vakvai bang in, huai bang in amun a kipan mi avakvai hi.
english: As a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man who wanders from his home.

paite: Nuh theih leh gimnamtui in lungtang akipaksak a; huai bangmah in mihing lawm khumna lungsimtak a thupha a hong pai ahi.
english: Perfume and incense bring joy to the heart; so does earnest counsel from a man’s friend.

paite: Na lawm mahmah, na pa lawm mangngilh ke'n; na tuahsiatna ni in na unau inn ah hoh ke'n; gamlapi a-unau sang in inveng nai om ahoihzaw hi.
english: Don’t forsake your friend and your father’s friend. Don’t go to your brother’s house in the day of your disaster. A neighbor who is near is better than a distant brother.

paite: Ka tapa, pil in, ka lungtang kipaksak in, kei hon taite ka dawntheihna ding in.
english: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, then I can answer my tormentor.

paite: Mipilvang in hoih lou amu a, abu hi; himahleh mimawl in a- awlmoh kei a, athuakloh hi.
english: A prudent man sees danger and takes refuge; but the simple pass on, and suffer for it.

paite: Mikhual a ding moh khu dia om puansilh la in; huan numei lamdang a dia moh khu dia om chiamkhamna ding in len in.
english: Take his garment when he puts up collateral for a stranger. Hold it for a wayward woman!

paite: Kuapeuh aw ngaihtaka, zingsang beltak a thou a, a-inveng vualzawl, ama a ding in hamsia a sim ahi ding hi.
english: He who blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be taken as a curse by him.

paite: Vuahchiin ni a vuah zu leh numei kinak hat akibang.
english: A continual dropping on a rainy day and a contentious wife are alike:

paite: Kuapeuh amah khou huih khou bang ahi a, khut taklam a sathau ham bang ahi.
english: restraining her is like restraining the wind, or like grasping oil in his right hand.

paite: Sik in sik ahiamsak bang in mihing in alawm mel ahiamsak hi.
english: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.

paite: Kuapeuh theipi kung kem in huai a agah ane ding; huan kuapeuh apu ngak zahtak in a-om ding hi.
english: Whoever tends the fig tree shall eat its fruit. He who looks after his master shall be honored.

paite: Tui a maitang in maitang amuh bang in, huai mah bang in mihing lungsim ah mihinna akimu hi.
english: Like water reflects a face, so a man’s heart reflects the man.

paite: Sheol leh Abaddon alungkim ngei kei ua, huan mihing mitte alungkim ngei kei uh.
english: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; and a man’s eyes are never satisfied.

paite: Huansianna bel dangka a ding ahi, huan meipi dangka-eng a ding, huchibang mah in mihing phatna a ze-et in a-om hi.
english: The crucible is for silver, and the furnace for gold; but man is refined by his praise.

paite: Mihai sum sung ah buh taisate lak ah suk in su mah lechin, huchipi in leng amah a kipan in ahaina apaimang kei lai ding hi.
english: Though you grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with grain, yet his foolishness will not be removed from him.

paite: Na belamhonte omdan thei ding in thanuam in, na ganhonte hoihtak in en in;
english: Know well the state of your flocks, and pay attention to your herds,

paite: Hauhsaknate tangtawn a ding ahi kei a; lallukhu in suan tengteng adaih zou hia?
english: for riches are not forever, nor does the crown endure to all generations.

paite: Buhpawl puak in a-om a, huan loupa nou akilang, mualte a loupate akilakhawm hi.
english: The hay is removed, and the new growth appears, the grasses of the hills are gathered in.

paite: Belamnoute'n na puansilh ding ahon pe ding, huan kelte'n na lou man ding.
english: The lambs are for your clothing, and the goats are the price of a field.

paite: Huan na an ding in, na inkote an ding in kel nawitui kiching a-om ding hi; huan na nungakte vakna ding in.
english: There will be plenty of goats’ milk for your food, for your family’s food, and for the nourishment of your servant girls.
